title: fix(ui): preserve Unicode boundaries in tool-stream status truncation
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Control UI chat truncated retry status messages and provider fallback model labels with raw `slice(0, 256)`. An emoji straddling that UTF-16 boundary left a dangling high surrogate, rendered as �.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse `truncateUtf16Safe` and the existing UI `truncateText` helper. Short text and the 256-unit ASCII limit stay unchanged; a split surrogate pair is excluded rather than corrupted.

Preserves nocodet888-arch's implementation and credit. Merged main at `fb84dd57fd5`, including #165580's test cleanup; moved the focused regression into the surviving `tool-stream.node.test.ts` suite instead of restoring the deleted startup suite.

No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

## Evidence

A built, isolated Gateway served the actual Control UI to Chromium in Docker. The UI sent a real chat run through the Codex harness to a scripted app-server provider. Its `model/rerouted` notification supplied a fallback model label containing 255 BMP units followed by an emoji. The Gateway projected the provider-policy notice over its real WebSocket; no browser event injection or hand-rendered component was used.

The screenshot fixture uses `fallback-` plus 246 spaces before the emoji: HTML collapses those spaces, making the cutoff visible without changing the 256-unit input boundary.

- **Before:** main's two truncation sites, on the merged runtime: captured DOM ends the label with `\ud83d`, painted as �.
- **After:** candidate: DOM contains no dangling surrogate or replacement character; the label ends cleanly at `fallback-`.
- Retry status, model and fallback model are also covered through `handleAgentEvent`. The regression fails on main's raw slicing and passes on the candidate.
- Short emoji-containing text is unchanged; 257 ASCII characters still produce exactly 256 characters.
- Targeted command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run ui/src/pages/chat/tool-stream.node.test.ts`. Candidate: 22 tests passed. Base: surrogate regression failed, 21 passed. The scoped run takes about two seconds including the runner; no new browser tests are added to CI.
- Gateway and UI builds completed inside the isolated container.
- The same real-browser path also passed the short-label and 270-character ASCII controls; ASCII output was exactly 256 characters.
- Live gate on `c58992e2a67d1ade1ee0bb946b1a623736453a54`: one real `gpt-5-mini` turn through the candidate Gateway, reasoning low, configured output budget 4096. Result: `LIVE_GATE_OK`, status `ok`, 17,567 input tokens and 137 output tokens (128 reasoning).
- The final commit only orders the added import; UI rebuild and the 22-test suite passed again. The previously captured browser behavior is unchanged.

### Before

![Before: fallback label shows a replacement glyph](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f804f8b2-ad44-4a65-a26f-be14409f1446)

### After

![After: fallback label truncates cleanly](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5141951d-2a14-4b64-8f83-20fbc4abc759)

Browser proof covers the fallback-label path. Current retry producers emit fixed short messages, so the long retry-message boundary is exercised by the regression test rather than claimed as a live provider retry.

## User Impact

Long retry status and provider-policy model labels remain valid Unicode at the cutoff. No configuration, protocol, stored-data or permission changes.

- [x] AI-assisted (Cursor and maintainer tooling)
- [x] I understand what the code does
- [x] Change is focused and does not mix unrelated concerns
